query: What numerical recipes produce stable differentiable finite-time Lyapunov exponent estimates on 2–10 s noisy windows and how to quantify their bias and variance?

response.query: What numerical recipes produce stable differentiable finite-time Lyapunov exponent estimates on 2–10 s noisy windows and how to quantify their bias and variance?
response.answer: The most stable differentiable finite-time Lyapunov exponent estimates on noisy windows use the Rosenstein algorithm. Bias and variance are quantified using bootstrap resampling techniques.
